newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Norilsk to transfer shares to government.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Norilsk to transfer shares to government.

text.p: Norilsk Nickel's board has taken a final decision to double the capital of its flagship plant and transfer the new controlling stake to the government, a spokesman said on Friday.
The spokesman said the company, a leading world producer of nickel and palladium group metals, would make the issue as part of a debt restructuring plan on federal tax arrears.
Norilsk said last month it owed workers at the flagship plant around 900 billion roubles ($156.8 million) and around 1.2 trillion roubles to various budgets.
Anatoly Komrakov, a spokesman for RAO Norilsky Nikel, said the board of directors had approved an issue of 11,020,269 ordinary shares for the unit at a meeting on Wednesday.
The Norilsk Mining and Metallurgical Complex has 11,020,268 common shares at present.

Komrakov said he was unable to say when the shares would be issued but that the Norilsk board was authorised to make the issue without approval of the main unit's shareholders, who are scheduled to meet on May 14. ($ = 5738 Russian Roubles)
